All three supplied HTML hashes exactly match upstream docs/pages files.
Sources: https://github.com/Cybersight-Security/Malware-Samples
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cybersight-Security/Malware-Samples/main/docs/js/script.js
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cybersight-Security/Malware-Samples/main/docs/styles/main.css
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Cybersight-Security/Malware-Samples/main/docs/assets/site.webmanifest
https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.4.0/css/all.min.css

No inline script, event handler, iframe, form submission, encoded payload,
non-ASCII concealment, executable binary header or trailing payload is present.
The script handles input by filtering a constant page list, then creates links
with textContent. Search text never leaves the browser. CSS imports Poppins
from Google Fonts; Font Awesome references only its relative webfonts. The
manifest declares names, start URL and icons, with no code or service worker.
GitHub sample-folder links require user navigation and do not execute malware.
Support and Discord links are ordinary anchors, not communications in code.
Current upstream dependency inspection cannot establish historical bytes.

Judgments: BENIGN, all three. Likely external-label hypothesis: repository-wide
malware labeling included documentation pages adjacent to real malware archives,
or a scanner classified the malware names and descriptive prose as behavior.

Generic backdoor text moves from webshell self-label to neutral vocabulary,
without changing matcher or scope. The old bare-vocabulary OR no longer emits
an objective: it is consolidated into its identified-panel consumer, preserving
the independent required panel label and both consumers' exclusions.
php-full-webshell explicitly retains the relocated member of its former selector.
direct-http-c2 deliberately loses bare-backdoor-vocabulary corroboration: a term
alone establishes no C2 role. CDN URL observations lose T1071.001 because asset
references do not establish C2.
Controls: vocabulary.html must match backdoor-term but not admin-terms-identified;
panel.html must match both; ordinary.html must match neither. Existing HTML
script/CDN observations remain notable. No sample name gates any rule.
